summary: Mark Rowe is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at McMaster University, where he is attested as an associate professor of religious studies in 2026.

Mark S. G. Dyczkowski (1951–2025) was an Indologist. He earned degrees at Banaras Hindu University, a PhD at Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Alexis Sanderson, and a DLitt at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, also studying under several traditional teachers.

Mark Siderits (born 1946) is a philosopher working in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as Emeritus Professor of Philosophy at Illinois State University (~1979–2008) and later at Seoul National University (~2008–2014).

Mark Singleton is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He completed an MPhil and PhD at the University of Cambridge, studying under Elizabeth De Michelis. He later held posts at St John's College (2007–2013) and SOAS (2015).

Mark T. Unno works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at Oberlin College and Stanford University, and held academic posts at Brown University and the University of Oregon (~2000).

Mark Tatz (1946–2021) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz and traditional teachers, and served as a professor at the California Institute of Integral Studies.

Mark Teeuwen (born 1966) is a scholar of Japanology and religious studies. He completed his MA and PhD at Leiden University, worked as a lecturer at Cardiff University (1994–1999), and became a professor at the University of Oslo in 1999.

Mark Wilks (1759–1831) was active in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Resident at the Kingdom of Mysore (~1803–1808), Governor of Saint Helena (~1813–1816), and became a Fellow of the Royal Society in 1826.
Mark William Carr (1833–1871) was an Indologist and linguist. His career included serving as Assistant Inspector General in the Madras Police (1862) and as a Major in the Madras Staff Corps (1870).
Mark Zebrowski (1944–1999) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his studies at Dartmouth College (~1962–1966) and Harvard University.
Markus Gabriel (born 1980) is a philosopher who studied at the University of Bonn. He held positions at Heidelberg, The New School, the University of Bonn, The New Institute, and Kyoto University.

Markus Viehbeck specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Vienna under Helmut Tauscher and Franz-Karl Ehrhard, and held researcher posts at Heidelberg University and the University of Vienna.

Marsha Weidner works in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After earning a PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, she held posts at the University of Virginia and the University of Kansas.

Marshall Livingston Perrin (1855–1935) was a linguist. He studied at Harvard and the University of Göttingen, where he also held a post. He later served as assistant professor and Professor of Sanskrit at Boston University.

Marshall Sahlins (1930–2021) was an anthropologist and historian. He studied at the University of Michigan and Columbia University, later holding faculty posts at the University of Michigan (~1957–1973) and the University of Chicago (1973).
Marta Bianco is a scholar in Sinology and Tibetology. She completed two master's degrees at the University of Naples "L'Orientale," where she also became a PhD candidate in 2024.

Marta Sanvido is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She held positions at Ca' Foscari University of Venice, UC Berkeley, the University of Hamburg, and became an assistant professor at Yale University in 2025.

Marta Sernesi is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Turin in 2007 and is attested as a Gastprofessorin at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2026.

Martha A. Muusses (1894–1981) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Utrecht University under Willem Caland and taught Dutch at Copenhagen, Stockholm, Uppsala, and Gothenburg universities.

Martha Ann Selby (born 1954) is an Indologist. She is Professor Emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin and serves at Harvard University as Sangam Professor of South Asian Studies, Professor of Comparative Literature, and department chair.
